column8: Wed 18 Nov: 3a store; twin of row 2 (the same NFF arts series, three in five at three months of cash or less before the pandemic); its only extra, 20% added to reserves while as many drew down, stays in the card.

Wed 18 Nov: 3a or 3d store; the pre-pandemic arts picture (61% at three months or less, 21% at six or more); the case's operating reserve is Laura's own set-aside for the ten (case l.94-95), so this is context for what co-sponsors call a reserve, beside H9-115.
Wed 18 Nov: store; NFF 2015 arts data and the under-one-month crisis line; never set 61% beside 39% as a recovery, since the bins changed wording (the row says so).
Wed 18 Nov: store only; NFF's 2009 figure is read only as Calabrese quotes it; read NFF 2010 before any use.

Wed 18 Nov: store; the use is NFF's own warning of probable voluntary response bias, so say surveyed groups, never the sector; the 50% and 19% rest on Irvin and Furneaux's quotation (chart image only).
Wed 18 Nov: store only; cash-rich groups beat their plans is a correlation, and the step to a residency planning to its programme is the card's, not the source's.
Wed 18 Nov: store; relief money lifted reserves for repeat respondents 2018-2022; pair with Q51-021 and H9-115 for the fall back, never alone.

Wed 18 Nov: 3a or 3d context; SeaChange Table 4C re-read at source today, the arts deciles match (median 0.1 months, 40th percentile 0.0); the case's reserve is Laura's set-aside, so contrast the kind of money (dated and owned), never the months.
Wed 18 Nov: 3a or 3e presentation; Tables 4A-4C re-read today (medians 3.4, 5.3, 0.1; 90th 20.6, 52.2, 27.4): one group, three yardsticks, so name the yardstick wherever a month figure is quoted.
Wed 18 Nov: 3d tone; the about half under one month headline re-read today; NPQ's tough status quo reading keeps the report from dramatising co-sponsors' thin reserves.
Wed 18 Nov: store; Calabrese's 39% with no reserve matches SeaChange's four in ten a decade apart; all nonprofits, not arts alone.

Wed 18 Nov: store; the NORI formula is new, but drop which is why her reserve is stated in her own books: the case itself sets the reserve aside in her portfolio (case l.94-95), so no funder ratio chose it.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e limit beside H9-119: the plan secures her ten payments, not the residency's own reserve (IPS l.11); Calabrese's link between sure public money and low reserves is a correlation, offered as a question co-sponsors may ask, not shown for founders.

Wed 18 Nov: 3a reason in one clause: even six months of reserves cannot hold a nonprofit's spending on trend through a bad patch (Calabrese 2018), while each of the ten is a dated Treasury paying $50,000 in every NUMBERS 8h world; site refused a re-read today, quote from the card.
Wed 18 Nov: store only; Blackwood and Pollak read only through two papers; read the Urban Institute original before any use.

Wed 18 Nov: 3d; the Sources list gives Calabrese (2011) as the Running on Empty working paper, but the five-times finding is likely his 2011 paper on donors and accumulated wealth: find and read it; ten years of her share is 10 x s budgets, not ten budgets; drop avoids that look as a design reason.

Wed 18 Nov: 3a or 3d context, corrects most to about four in ten for 2024; SMU's page re-read today says three months of expenses or less, 42% in 2024 against 56% pre-pandemic, so use that wording and one release's figure (41% in the tables).
Wed 18 Nov: store; one arts group in six held more than a year of its whole budget in 2024; never set beside her 120 months without her share named (row 31, H9-119).
Wed 18 Nov: store; small arts groups held more months than large ones (SMU), against Sloan et al.; a new residency's risk is thin income, not a thin balance.
Wed 18 Nov: 3e discipline; SMU's 2019 median is 1.5, 3.9 or 2.33 by release, so Q9-013's 1.5 must carry its release and year if it is ever quoted.
Wed 18 Nov: store; a pledged later year is a receivable restricted by time, so it sits outside unrestricted working capital: say that, never not a current asset (Q90 has the pledge accounting).

Wed 18 Nov: 3d; BBB Standard 10 re-read at give.org today, both quotes exact; say it as a fact about funders (donors expect money used for current needs), never as the plan's reason: the case puts the reserve in her portfolio (l.94-95) and the IPS holds Treasuries for l.11's certainty; drop the judge's note's never short (row 13).

Wed 18 Nov: store; Hong Kong's 25% ceiling and clawback for nine flagship troupes; Taiwan's co-sponsors are not shown to read reserves this way, so drop the guess about hoarding; LegCo PDF refused a re-read today (robots).
Wed 18 Nov: detail of row 23 (each troupe's ratio under the ceiling); store with it.

Wed 18 Nov: 3a framing in one clause: no accepted benchmark exists for arts reserves, so appropriate is a judgment the report makes by the reserve's job, the ten payments (case l.94-95); give the 2012 Hong Kong study as its context.

Wed 18 Nov: store; 20% and 25% are not one number: say about a fifth of a year is a floor for Australia's major companies and about a quarter a ceiling in Hong Kong; the team's Australian angle only if it earns its place.
Wed 18 Nov: store; England's funded arts groups' median eight weeks of free reserves and the median against average gap; the 2023 edition's wording contradicts itself, so 2018/19 only.
Wed 18 Nov: store only; an advocacy report's own six-month line; a reason not to boast, nothing more.
Wed 18 Nov: store only; UK arts centres run thin; venues with ticket income, far from a residency.
Wed 18 Nov: store; an audit firm's client list looks far richer than NFF or SMU, so who answers sets the typical months; a quoting rule, not a plan limit.

Wed 18 Nov: 3a or 3.0 wording; the thresholds check (3.4/120 = 2.8%, 27.4/120 = 22.8%, 52.2/120 = 43.5%, Keel arithmetic); H9-119's budgets put her share anywhere from about 1% to 45%, so say only ten years of the founder's own payments, never whole-budget months; supersedes Q9b-029's framing.

Wed 18 Nov: 3a and Figure 1's note; every figure reproduces from NUMBERS 8h re-sized Tue 17 Nov evening ($445,655; 111.7% of $399,089; $416,082; 113.3% to 251.9%), replacing Q9b-029's $444,545; a schedule that ends in 2042, never an endowment; ratio in Figure 1's note only (SKELETON 3a density row).

Wed 18 Nov: twin of Q16-038, which already holds NORI's not intended to replace a permanent loss of revenue and the designated-fund contrast; the two reasons here are reasons to change the plan (IPS l.17), fine as worded.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of Q55-008 and Q48-012 (later years earmarked, not promised); the owned against earmarked contrast is already in Q55-043's grid.

Wed 18 Nov: 3a or 3.0, sector evidence under the reserve aha Taiwan's founders had no year in hand (Q100-035, Q100-041): NCAF's 2009 study finds groups cannot keep much cash and use one show to feed the next; performing groups, 2005 figures, so say so.
Wed 18 Nov: store; small Taiwanese groups took 52-60% of income from public money in 2004-2008, the concentrated public funds Calabrese links to low reserves; old data.
Wed 18 Nov: NCAF's deficits are the norm restates the same 2005 survey as row 35; carry the phrase as row 35's clause, never as a second finding.
Wed 18 Nov: 3d; Taiwan's own advice, a 10-15% buffer (about 1.2-1.8 months, Keel arithmetic), the lowest norm here; one accountant at an NCAF workshop, so say advice, never a rule.
Wed 18 Nov: store; the outstanding-troupe grant is not shown to be multi-year, so say few won it (124 of 7,198, 1.72%, 2019-2024), never any multi-year money; drop the top sliver boast.

Wed 18 Nov: 3d and 2.3, residency-specific evidence for IPS l.9: in 2008-10 58% of Alliance residencies cut staff or pay, 46% and 58% saw foundation and individual giving fall, endowments of those that had them fell 29%, while some had double the applications; re-read at giarts.org today, exact; say can (card Q50), US members only.
Wed 18 Nov: store; residency counts and fees (2012), overlapping Q9-018's about 500; why founders' money matters is the card's inference.
